title: Route-level economics explainer service: canonicalize per-route cost & latency breakdowns
creator: Marco Hernandez
description:
Summary:
Build a new backend microservice — the Route Economics Explainer (REE) — that produces deterministic, explainable per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns used by Console dashboards, billing reports, and anomaly alerts. REE will be the canonical source for breakdowns (not a view-layer aggregation) and must align with serving runtime semantics (batching, KV cache hits, model variant fallbacks).

Goals:
- Produce line-item level decomposition for each request grouping: routing decision, model variant, batching allocation, prefix KV cache effect, transport overhead, kernel/sequence compute, and queuing delay.
- Emit both streaming (near-real-time) and daily rollups with identical math so that realtime charts and end-of-day reconciliations agree within tolerance.
- Make decomposition auditable: inputs to the math (raw telemetry) must be retained and linkable to the breakdown item.
- Provide a compact, queryable format for Console and billing services to consume without re-running expensive joins.

Design notes / approach:
1) Ingestion: REE will consume two primary streams: runtime traces (spans/events) and billing-enriched usage events (token counts, embedding units). Traces supply latency components (scheduling, execution, I/O); usage events supply tokenization and cost multipliers. An initial PoC will use the existing telemetry kafka topic "runtime-telemetry-v2" plus daily usage batch from the chargeback extractor.

2) Canonical keying: records keyed by (tenant_id, route_id, model_variant_id, request_id, day). This allows both per-request detail and deterministic daily aggregation. Request-level entries will include an attribution tag that shows which portion of the token stream contributed to which model/kernel stage (for example: prompt generation vs. streaming completion).

3) Attribution model: implement a two-pass attribution: primary attribution based on causal spans (preferred) and a fallback compositional attribution when spans are incomplete. Rules: KV cache hits subtract from compute token count; batched requests amortize scheduling and kernel startup overhead by token-equivalent weight; network transport is pro-rated per chunk boundary.

4) Cost mapping: map compute time to cost using a configurable unit rate table by runtime-pool (g4dn, a100x, quantized-cpu) and add license/premium multipliers for Dedicated customers. Config table exposed via Console infra-config service and used by REE for rollups.

5) Storage & query model: store per-request decompositions in a compact parquet-based materialization partitioned by day and tenant with a separate daily-rollup table pre-computed by Spark/Beam for fast Console reads. Retain raw request decompositions for 30 days and rollups for 3 years.

6) Reconciliation: provide a reconciliation job that compares per-request sum to daily rollup and emits a reconciliation score and diagnostics to Sentry/Telemetry when divergence exceeds 0.5%.

7) API contract: a small read API (gRPC) for Console that returns: breakdown_items (ordered list), total_cost, total_latency_ms, source_hash (to tie back to raw telemetry). Include explainability text snippets describing applied heuristics.

Acceptance criteria:
- REE produces daily rollups for 90% of routes within 48 hours of ingest during the rollout phase.
- Console displays breakdowns that match billing prototype within 0.5% for aggregate tenant totals in tests across three load profiles.
- Regression tests for span-less fallback logic cover at least 85% of synthetic failure cases.
- Reconciliation job detects and alerts on divergences >0.5% with human-readable diagnostic payload.

Non-goals:
- REE will not (in this phase) attempt to infer customer-level pricing tiers beyond applying configured multipliers.
- REE will not serve as the authoritative billing ledger — it produces explainable breakdowns; the billing system remains the source of truth for invoices.

Rollout plan / milestones:
- Week 0: schema design + unit test harness for attribution rules (spans + fallback).
- Week 1: lightweight PoC that consumes telemetry and emits per-request decompositions to a dev partition.
- Week 2: implement cost-rate table integration, API for Console, and reconciliation job.
- Week 3: internal dogfood (select tenants), run reconciliation and refine heuristics.
- Week 4: cut a beta release flagged for Console dev org, collect feedback, finalize reliability SLOs.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Accuracy vs availability: causal-span attribution is more accurate but brittle; fallback heuristics increase availability. We'll track confidence at item level so Console can indicate low-confidence breakdowns.
- Storage costs: per-request retention at high QPS will be storage-heavy. Mitigation: compact encoding, coalescing identical decompositions, and retention tiering.
- Cross-service schema drift: runtime must adopt a minimal stable telemetry contract. If runtime fields change, REE will default to conservative attribution and emit schema-mismatch diagnostics.

Operational metrics to add:
- ingestion_lag_seconds (p95/p99), daily_rollup_latency_hours, reconciliation_divergence_pct, per-tenant_storage_bytes, explainability_confidence_dist.

Links / artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Route+Economics+Explainer+Design
- PoC notebooks: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/route-econ-poc
- Example Console mockup: https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ/route-econ-console
- Related tickets: ENG-7421 (previous aggregator proto), ENG-9234 (telemetry chargeback pipeline), ENG-20489 (billing insights rollup engine)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Daily rollups produced and reconciled within tolerance; 2) Console reads fast (<300ms median) for tenant-level queries; 3) Reconciliation alerts fire and contain diagnostics; 4) End-to-end tests for both span-backed and fallback attribution pass in CI.
